# Independent review: catalogue v7

## Verdict

**PASS_WITH_QUALIFICATIONS** for candidate **`b303210af5d4f8395044bb8cd31508d7ee801b4640704c1253a433e68e1c88d3`**, generated by branch `catalogue-v7`, commit **`75a395b551042f30d2cb89169b0a58b400842fbe`**.

All eight proposed boundaries are independently supported under the repository's `armlink5-inline-branchnop-v2` model. No new false split, lost entry, changed protected record, extent imbalance, or additional missed boundary satisfying the new rules was found. The qualification concerns the generality of the helper's ABI return-class model, not the eight boundaries in this image. There are **no blocker or major findings**.

This is an independent denominator review, not adoption, a source/interface review, or accepted C progress. No tracked file was written, no commit was made, and no build or test module other than `tests.test_analyze` was run. All review writes are beneath `scratch/review/catalogue-v7/` in the main checkout. Private packets contain original material and must not be published; this report contains only metadata and instruction-class conclusions.

## Findings

| ID | Severity | Subject | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V7-R01 | note | ABI result classes are not a general AAPCS whitelist | `tools/analyze.py:1190,1217-1221` models alternative results as core `r0` or VFP `s0-s7`. This is sufficient for the **observed new mixed `r0` + VFP witnesses**, but not every legal AAPCS result: base-PCS double-word results use `r0-r1`, and 128-bit containerized results use `r0-r3`. The core limitation predates v7's changes. On SIMD targets, homogeneous 128-bit-vector aggregates can also use more than `s0-s7`; that extension is outside this repository's MPCore target. [INFERENCE] Reusing the helper as a general ABI proof without widening/qualifying those classes could misclassify a legal result use as pass-through arguments. None of the eight new splits relies on that case, and no denominator correction is required here. |
| V7-R02 | note | Section identity versus original source identity | The evidence establishes separable callable sections **under the adopted linker/ABI model**. [INFERENCE] The eight successors were separate original ARMCC/armlink functions. Original source spelling, declarations, semantic correctness, and whether adjacency came from source order or `--tailreorder` are not established by this review. |

ABI cross-check: Arm's [AAPCS32 specification](https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa/blob/main/aapcs32/aapcs32.rst), sections **VFP register usage conventions**, **Result Return (base PCS)**, **VFP co-processor register candidates**, and **Result return (VFP variant)**. It confirms D/S overlap, caller-saved `s0-s15` versus callee-saved `s16-s31`, scalar/HFA VFP results, and the result-class qualifications above. Target scope is `config/compiler_profiles.json` / `docs/COMPILER.md`: `--cpu=MPCore`.

## Code review: guards and new rules

I compared the full patch with the v6 rules in `docs/catalogue/REPORT-v6.md`, then independently decoded the changed owners and inspected paired private packet structures. The author report was a claims checklist, not the source of the derived structure or preservation totals.

### V6 false-split guards

The following remain active:

- Only the exact executed, unconditional architectural instruction class identified by the linker model is eligible. Scheduling NOP hints, predicated alternatives, data and the unexecuted switch slot are not substitutes.
- This remains the last partitioning pass. There is no new discovery/refinement after cutting extents.
- Actual saved-stack LR is tracked separately from the frozen census's textual LR flag. Conditional restores do not establish the new restored-frame witness. Newly recognized single LR loads require the matching saved slot; balanced SP and no intervening LR overwrite are required for the new setter evidence.
- All direct forward/backward branch crossings and address-switch crossings retain their veto. Literal/pool ownership crossings and unresolved literal conflicts retain theirs.
- Existing entry addresses are retained; a partition containing an additional interior entry is still rejected.
- Protected ownership is compared against **whole adopted records**. A changed proposal is withheld, and failure to retain the expected record still raises an error. Adoption-safe regeneration remains covered by the inherited tests and the new-evidence test.

No v6 false-split guard was weakened for the proposed revision. The intentional extensions are the expanded live-register witness and candidate admission for independently matched actual frame restores; the latter adds **zero actual-image candidates** outside the frozen tail cohort.

### New VFP witness

The D-to-two-S-lane normalization is correct for this target, including partial S writes. Explicit register-list semantics repair Capstone's missing VSTM/VLDM accesses. Callee-saved lanes do not become argument witnesses. Conditional writes are not treated as unconditional initialization, and a flags-only dependency remains insufficient.

The six actual successors read an untouched core object pointer **and** pass-through VFP lanes before those lanes are initialized. The incompatible *simultaneous* core/VFP live state, rather than an `s0` read alone, is decisive. Neither a core result nor a scalar/HFA VFP result explains that state under AAPCS-VFP. All six heads are stack-independent leaves with no LR overwrite. The two more complex suffixes at `0x0015e4a8` and `0x0015e634` have their own later conditional control flow, but the mixed witness is established before it, and no branch or PC-relative data reference crosses either cut.

### New restored-frame setter witness

For both actual setters I independently symbolically paired the stack register-list save and restore: LR is restored from its original slot **entry-SP minus 4**, SP is back at entry value at the tail site, and LR is not overwritten afterward. The suffix initializes its temporary register, performs a fixed-offset word field store through unchanged `r0`, and returns. It is three instructions / 12 bytes, exactly closes the old owner, and has no stack, call, predication, literal, indexed-addressing or callee-saved-register dependency.

Under `docs/LINKER.md`, a call erased by armlink cannot explain a post-restore tail site followed by this return: an original BL there would overwrite the just-restored return address. The next-instruction tail-branch model explains both cases. The implementation does not generalize this to an arbitrary post-epilogue suffix.

- **Every v6 owner and callable start/entry is preserved in the same ISA.** Removed owners and lost address/ISA pairs are both empty.
- Exactly eight old records change, exactly eight successors are added, and **4,564 old owner records are identical**. The changed owners and added starts are precisely the table above.
- All **129** v6 internal-tail cut sites remain present; v7 has **137**. All **270** frozen `(site,census_class)` pairs are identical.
- Independently merged interval sets for code, pools and literals are identical. Every range-kind coverage set is identical: function, unknown, data, rodata, padding and segment padding. The map still tiles the same mapped segments; `validate_catalogue` returns **`[]`**.
- All anomaly records and literal-conflict records are identical, not only their counts. The eight old extents total **480 bytes**, partitioned as **176 head bytes + 304 successor bytes**.
- Every changed head and successor exceeds the linker's eight-byte inlining limit. All other function records are identical, so these cuts do not change tiny-original-callee eligibility.

## Search for missed or false cases

An independent raw aligned-word address scan confirms the complete **776-site** inventory. Its dispositions are:

| Disposition | Sites |
| --- | ---: |
| Applied internal split | 137 |
| Already separate | 86 |
| Crossing control flow | 31 |
| Crossing literal/data ownership | 1 |
| No independent successor witness | 7 |
| Unowned tail without an established head | 8 |
| Excluded in-frame call | 505 |
| Unexecuted switch slot | 1 |
| **Total** | **776** |

I inspected all seven still-unwitnessed suffixes and extended the live probe past the implementation's 12-instruction bound to the first control transfer for those suffixes and all **505** excluded in-frame sites. **No additional live-argument witness was found**, including beyond the normal bound. The retained successors are `0x0010bef4`, `0x00131950`, `0x001c5640`, `0x001d0348`, `0x001d2234`, `0x001efcd8`, and `0x001f478c`.

Their instruction-class structures explain the retention: branch-only or load/tail suffixes, core-only result-compatible use, a longer non-field-store suffix, or conditional/calling bodies rather than a closed restored-frame setter. None supplies the new mixed core/VFP witness; none satisfies the new short setter predicate. The control/data-crossing populations retain their veto. No additional actual restore outside the census introduces a candidate in this image. No new split looks false under the adopted model.

These are bounded model-based findings, not a claim that every still-merged owner in the image is a single original source function. The seven deliberately conservative retentions are not failures of the new rules.
